top.title: Report – Milan Owner Gerry Cardinale Makes Real Madrid Starlet His Priority Ahead of Tresoldi
top.description: Report – Milan Owner Gerry Cardinale Makes Real Madrid Starlet His Priority Ahead of Tresoldi Milan appear to have settled on Endrick as their preferred attacking target for January, with Gerry Cardinale reportedly favouring the Real Madrid youngster over Nicolo Tresoldi. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Rossoneri owner has personally accelerated the pursuit of the Brazilian after publicly expressing his admiration for the 20-year-old. Cardinale left little doubt about his intentions when discussing the transfer market, describing Endrick as one of the most gifted youngsters in the world in his position, if not the most talented. The Brazilian has struggled for regular playing time at the Santiago Bernabeu, accumulating just 160 minutes between La Liga and the Champions League this season. However, Jose Mourinho remains reluctant to sanction Endrick’s departure, considering he has been an important part of his plans at Real Madrid. Endrick is also reportedly happy in the Spanish capital, meaning Milan could face considerable obstacles in their pursuit. Milan Chief Prefers Endrick to Tresoldi Although Nicolo Tresoldi remains on Milan’s shortlist, Cardinale considers Endrick a more attractive option because of his versatility. The Real Madrid forward can operate as a center-forward, a right-sided attacker or an attacking midfielder, making him a potentially valuable addition to Ruben Amorim’s tactical system. By contrast, Tresoldi offers a more traditional center-forward profile, potentially complicating his integration alongside Goncalo Ramos. The Club Brugge youngster has also attracted Bayern Munich’s attention, particularly following Harry Kane’s injury. Milan could nevertheless benefit from Cardinale’s strong relationship with Roc Nation, the agency representing Endrick. A loan move or a permanent transfer with a buy-back clause could emerge as possible solutions, although much will depend on Real Madrid’s willingness to negotiate.

top.title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
top.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him. The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation. The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets. He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced. “Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said. Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways. He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation. The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims. He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence. In hindsight, the contract Shamet signed to return to the Knicks is looking like a bargain for New York — and it's no coincidence New York has started to look like the team it was last season with him rolling. top.title: Otti begins construction of new Umuahia traffic corridor
top.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas. The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capital Development Authority (UCDA), is designed to provide an alternative traffic corridor, ease congestion around Government House and Isigate, and improve connectivity within the state capital. The General Manager of UCDA, Engr. Kingsley Agomoh, who conducted journalists round the project site, said the road would allow motorists coming from Bende and Ikot Ekpene roads to connect to Abia Line, Aguiyi Ironsi Boulevard, Abia Express Tower and Onuimo Road without passing through the Government House axis. He said the project would significantly reduce traffic pressure on major roads, stimulate economic activities and improve the aesthetics of Umuahia. ” If you are coming from Bende Road, you pass through the Post Office Tower, cross the railway station and connect to First Bank, Ridge Club and Abia Line without going through the Government House axis,” Agomoh said. He explained that the project was part of Otti’s broader urban renewal programme, adding that the governor had also directed the relocation of Umuahia Railway Station to the Nnennaya Oti Bus Terminal. According to him, the state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Railway Corporation to facilitate the construction of the access road across the railway corridor. Agomoh also disclosed that another road linking First Bank to the Keystone, Sterling and FCMB bank areas would be reopened and reconstructed to provide motorists, particularly those coming from the Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia, with a shorter alternative route. He said the road, which had been encroached upon by adjoining property owners, was being reclaimed to restore access and ease movement within the commercial district. Describing the railway-crossing road as a signature project of the Otti administration, Agomoh said the governor’s urban renewal drive was repositioning Umuahia for increased economic activities and orderly development. He urged Abians to support Otti and other Labour Party candidates in the 2027 elections, arguing that continuity would ensure the completion of ongoing infrastructure projects across the state. top.title: Dallas Cowboys fan from New Mexico dies after 49ers game altercation
top.description: Arlington police are looking into the death of a lifelong Dallas Cowboys fan days following an alleged altercation around kickoff during the game against the San Francisco 49ers, USA Today reported. The family of Mario Narro contacted police on Tuesday, Nov. 17, about the incident. Narro died on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Narro, 36, had traveled from Albuquerque to attend the NFC rivalry game when an alleged alteration with a 49ers fan ended when Narro was pushed and fell down a flight of stairs, his family told CBS News Texas and the California Post , a branch of the New York Post. His family said he had a swollen abdomen and bruising and sat through the game, but wasn't feeling well. He was taken to a stadium medical team, who then transported him to a hospital. He had multiple surgeries and died on Wednesday, Nov. 18. An official cause of death is pending. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones spoke about the fan's death on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Friday, Nov. 20. Jones said there was no record of the incident but the organization was looking into it. Jones added that the Cowboys would cooperate with authorities for any surveillance footage or information the team could find. "Let me make the point of, we really do have quite eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago, we have quite a surveillance of what's going on in every aspect of our game," Jones said. "So it is really rare if we didn't know of any incident. We've got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day." top.title: Dwight Howard Regrets Rejecting Stephen Curry Trade In 2011 And Passing On Warriors In 2013
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-USA TODAY Sports Dwight Howard regrets missing two opportunities to play alongside Stephen Curry , revealing that he opposed the Orlando Magic’s interest in acquiring the guard in 2011 before choosing the Houston Rockets over the Golden State Warriors in 2013. Speaking with Casey Kiernan on The AM Hoops Show , Howard admitted that he failed to recognize what Curry would become. At the time, he preferred Curry’s more established backcourt partner, Monta Ellis . “But I had an opportunity to play with Steph too, and I’m tripping. At the time, I wanted to play with Monta Ellis.” “The Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph, and I said no. I said no because I didn’t know Wardell Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest shooters in the world. At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes. I regret it…” Howard’s recollection describes a potential acquisition discussed with Orlando’s front office. It does not establish that the Warriors had agreed to a completed trade or that Howard formally possessed veto authority. Nevertheless, he clearly believes his preference helped close off an intriguing possibility. The numbers explain why Ellis appealed to him. In 2010-11, Ellis averaged 24.1 points and 5.6 assists while playing 40.3 minutes per game. Curry averaged 18.6 points and 5.8 assists in 33.6 minutes, although his 44.2% three-point shooting already demonstrated exceptional potential. Ellis was the more prominent scorer; Curry was still developing into the player who would transform basketball. Howard eventually left Orlando for the Los Angeles Lakers in 2012. nigeria.title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him. The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation. The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets. He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced. “Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said. Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways. He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation. The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims. He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence. nigeria.title: Otti begins construction of new Umuahia traffic corridor
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas. The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capital Development Authority (UCDA), is designed to provide an alternative traffic corridor, ease congestion around Government House and Isigate, and improve connectivity within the state capital. The General Manager of UCDA, Engr. Kingsley Agomoh, who conducted journalists round the project site, said the road would allow motorists coming from Bende and Ikot Ekpene roads to connect to Abia Line, Aguiyi Ironsi Boulevard, Abia Express Tower and Onuimo Road without passing through the Government House axis. He said the project would significantly reduce traffic pressure on major roads, stimulate economic activities and improve the aesthetics of Umuahia. ” If you are coming from Bende Road, you pass through the Post Office Tower, cross the railway station and connect to First Bank, Ridge Club and Abia Line without going through the Government House axis,” Agomoh said. He explained that the project was part of Otti’s broader urban renewal programme, adding that the governor had also directed the relocation of Umuahia Railway Station to the Nnennaya Oti Bus Terminal. According to him, the state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Railway Corporation to facilitate the construction of the access road across the railway corridor. Agomoh also disclosed that another road linking First Bank to the Keystone, Sterling and FCMB bank areas would be reopened and reconstructed to provide motorists, particularly those coming from the Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia, with a shorter alternative route. He said the road, which had been encroached upon by adjoining property owners, was being reclaimed to restore access and ease movement within the commercial district. Describing the railway-crossing road as a signature project of the Otti administration, Agomoh said the governor’s urban renewal drive was repositioning Umuahia for increased economic activities and orderly development. He urged Abians to support Otti and other Labour Party candidates in the 2027 elections, arguing that continuity would ensure the completion of ongoing infrastructure projects across the state. nigeria.title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
nigeria.description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja. The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children. Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together. He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter. “Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said. He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court. The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano. “Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said. Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details. Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react. “I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked. He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him. The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15. The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings. The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress. nigeria.title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, extend La Liga lead
nigeria.description: Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. “We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.” The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide. The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up. – Quickfire treble – Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute. Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated. “The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN. Later Sunday Atletico Madrid, third, visit Getafe among other fixtures. Vanguard News The post Barcelona

nigeria.title: Katsina ADC Gov Candidate Kaita Launches 2027 Campaign
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Katsina State, Senator Ahmed Kaita, has officially launched his 2027 campaign in the Funtua senatorial zone, drawing a crowd of supporters as residents of Funtua Local Government pledged to back ADC candidates in all elective positions during the forthcoming general elections. The campaign rally, held on Sunday at Aya Primary School in Funtua, attracted scores of supporters from across Funtua and neighbouring communities, signalling the party’s determination to mount a strong challenge in the state. Addressing the crowd, Senator Kaita expressed gratitude for what he described as the overwhelming voluntary turnout of supporters, insisting that those in attendance were driven by a genuine desire for change and good governance rather than political inducement. The event attracted scores of supporters from across Funtua and neighbouring communities. He said the campaign would unveil its comprehensive policy agenda during the next rally scheduled for Faskari Local Government Area on Tuesday, explaining that the decision was deliberate to distinguish the ADC’s approach from that of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). “Today marks the beginning of the change that Katsina people have been yearning for. Everyone you see here came willingly because they desire good governance. I sincerely appreciate our supporters for the warm reception. By the grace of God, we will unveil our agenda in Faskari on Tuesday. We want to show the difference between our campaign and that of the APC-led government,” Kaita declared. Before proceeding to the rally venue, the ADC governorship candidate paid a courtesy visit to the Sarkin Maskan Katsina and District Head of Funtua, where he sought royal blessings, prayers, guidance and support ahead of the elections. The event also featured the ADC senatorial candidate for Funtua zone, Hon. Jamilu Muhammad Lion, whose appearance drew loud cheers from the large gathering of party faithful. The Funtua rally marks the first major campaign outing by Senator Kaita in the 2027 election season and sets the stage for the ADC’s statewide mobilisation as political activities gather momentum across Katsina State. nigeria.title: Bayern’s Musiala suffered another seizure this week
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich and Germany midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered another previously undisclosed seizure this week, according to information received by AFP subsidiary SID on Sunday. The incident, which is categorised by a brief and temporary loss of consciousness or awareness, occurred at training on Monday. Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Monday’s incident was the second since Musiala’s announcement, with the player reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play. News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union FIFPRO for a “coordinated campaign” to pressure the Germany international to renegotiate his 2025-extended contract. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. nigeria.title: Taraba Yoruba community endorses Tinubu, Kefas for second term
nigeria.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO – The Yoruba Community Council (YCC) in Taraba State has endorsed President Bola Tinubu and Governor Agbu Kefas for a second term in office, expressing confidence in their leadership and commitment to peace, security and development. The President of the council, Mr Joseph Abiodun Durojaye, announced the endorsement at the 2026 Yoruba Day celebration held over the weekend in Jalingo. The event brought together Yoruba residents from Oyo, Osun, Lagos, Ondo, Kwara, Ogun, Kogi and Ekiti states, among others. Durojaye expressed appreciation to the Kefas administration for its support and goodwill towards the Yoruba community, particularly the appointment of one of its members as a Special Adviser and financial assistance towards the construction of the Yoruba Community Council building. He appealed for continued government support to ensure the completion of the project, saying the building would serve as a permanent centre for community meetings, cultural activities, youth development and other programmes. The community leader formally declared the council’s support for Kefas’s re-election bid, subject to the democratic process and the decision of the electorate. He also expressed support for Tinubu’s re-election for another four-year term. nigeria.title: Crude supply to refineries hits 179.31m barrels in 10 months
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Crude oil supply to domestic refineries in Nigeria reached 179.31 million barrels between January and October 2026, with local production accounting for 144.97 million barrels and imports contributing 34.33 million barrels. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), in its October 2026 Midstream and Downstream Statistics, disclosed that crude oil supply to refineries rose to 22.8 million barrels in October, from 18.53 million barrels in September. The October figure represented a 23.1 per cent increase month-on-month. A breakdown showed that domestic crude supply increased by 19.8 per cent to 19.13 million barrels in October, from 15.97 million barrels in the preceding month. Similarly, imported crude supply rose by 43.4 per cent to 3.67 million barrels in October, compared with 2.56 million barrels in September. Meanwhile, the daily average receipt of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, increased by 21 per cent to 46.9 million litres per day in October, from 38.7 million litres per day in September. According to the report, domestic refineries supplied an average of 31.9 million litres of petrol daily in October, compared with 28.5 million litres per day in September, representing a 12 per cent increase. Petrol imports also increased by 47 per cent to 15 million litres per day in October, from 10.2 million litres per day in the preceding month. Despite the improvement, total petrol supply remained below the estimated daily demand benchmark of 50 million litres and the 13-month average of 50.2 million litres per day. The report further showed that domestic refineries accounted for 62.6 per cent of the 13-month average petrol supply, while imports contributed 37.4 per cent. A month-by-month breakdown indicated that domestic refinery petrol supply peaked at 41.5 million litres per day in May, while imports reached their highest level of 24.8 million litres per day in January. Combined petrol receipts peaked at 74.2 million litres per day in December 2025 before declining in subsequent months. On other petroleum products, the NMDPRA report showed that daily average receipts of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), commonly known as diesel, increased by 93 per cent to 16.8 million litres per day in October. However, aviation fuel (ATK) receipts declined by 36 per cent to 2.1 million litres per day, while Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) receipts increased by 11 per cent to 5.2 thousand tonnes daily. entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. Turkish Airlines: Turn Istanbul Into Part of Your Holiday Turkish Airlines operates a Stopover in Istanbul programme for eligible international passengers connecting through Istanbul Airport. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? entertainment.title: International Men’s Day: Six Films That Explore the Vulnerable Side of Men
entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. sports.title: Chris Berman announces Tom Jackson’s death in emotional tribute on ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’
sports.description: Chris Berman grew emotional Sunday while discussing Tom Jackson, his longtime ESPN broadcast partner, who died Friday at 75 . “He was a vital 75,” Berman said on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” show. “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.” Berman, who said he spoke “at length” to Jackson as recently as Tuesday, also called the former Broncos linebacker “one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.” He quoted The Temptations hit song “My Girl,” saying Jackson always “brought sunshine on a cloudy day.” Chris Berman remembers his longtime broadcast partner and dear friend, Tom Jackson, following his passing. pic.twitter.com/4pufldOXSV — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 22, 2026 ESPN commentators Tom Jackson and Chris Berman cover the game between the Chicago Bears and St. Louis Rams in St. Louis, Missouri, Dec. 11, 2006. Getty Images “All of us are stunned,” Berman read from a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro added that Jackson — a three-time Pro Bowler over 14 NFL seasons with the Broncos — was “one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history.” “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans,” Pitaro said. “Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact. Sports anchors Chris Berman, left, and Tom Jackson speak during a ceremony honoring Berman with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in Hollywood, Calif. Getty Images “Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.” Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 but returned for a digital edition of “NFL Primetime” alongside Berman in 2019. He had been awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015, an honor which Berman also had earned in 2010. Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that . science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo mission becomes 2nd ever to arrive in orbit around Mercury
science.description: null For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. Flight Dynamics already has confirmed it achieved orbital capture around Mercury! Early next week we'll share the next update with the upcoming steps," the mission team said via X on Saturday evening. We've heard back from Bepi - the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC are busy assessing the telemetry. Flight Dynamics already has confirmed it achieved orbital capture around Mercury!Early next week we'll share the next update with the upcoming steps. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies.
